executive_assessment.text: Hanang event losses, Kilosa drainage obstruction and Rufiji/Msembe hydrology provide geographically specific evidence with distinct methods and periods.

Selected councils show preparedness gaps; Kilosa conflict material and Monduli/Longido governance findings are abstract-only. Chamwino/Mpwapwa plans and approved finance add capacity, not evaluated effects.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-03 reports: The audit's cited July 2024 report says the 2023 Hanang mudslide affected 261 houses, destroyed 95, damaged 754.875 acres of farmland and disrupted 742 businesses.
Source dated 2025-03 reports: In Kilosa, auditors observed a Standard Gauge Railway stormwater culvert without a continuous downstream channel; accumulated floodwater affected neighboring areas.

Source dated 2025-03 reports: In 2024, none of five visited councils had demarcated or protected identified flood-prone areas; the audit tables show no disaster-coordination allocations in Kinondoni, Hanang, Mbeya or Kilosa, unlike Rufiji.
The ministry's 2024 sector report describes above-average Rufiji rainfall and high Great Ruaha flow at Msembe during the 2023–2024 season.

Source dated 2021 reports: A 2021 cross-sectional study of 120 respondents in selected Kilosa wards and villages reports farmer-pastoralist conflict over land, water and pasture and attributes resource scarcity partly to climate variability.

Source dated 2025 reports: A 2025 mixed-methods study across Monduli and Longido reports that responsiveness, accountability, transparency and stakeholder participation significantly influenced local adaptation implementation, with participation strongest.

Source dated not stated reports: The Dodoma project describes its Chamwino and Mpwapwa target communities as groundwater-dependent; unreliable rainfall affects crops and livestock and is associated with drought, flooding, erosion and limited recharge.

Source dated not stated reports: The completed project reports community-led plans adopted by Chamwino and Mpwapwa councils, 25 adaptation actions added to 2024/25 plans and budgets, and TZS 500 million approved for implementation.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 18 of 18 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The opened Tanzania sources report climate risks and development vulnerabilities but do not establish a country-specific climate-to-conflict or climate-to-violence link.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.

The only accessible study directly stating climate variability contributes to farmer-pastoralist conflict in Kilosa was a 2021 repository abstract; full text, named wards, conflict prevalence and causal identification were unavailable.
A separate study argues farmer-herder conflict in Rufiji and Kisarawe is shaped by pastoral land-access exclusion, but its publisher full text returned 403; it was not used as evidence.
No inspected source documented insecurity or violence preventing a named adaptation activity; local flooding preparedness gaps are not treated as FCV constraints.
Government flood audit figures are scoped to selected councils and 2020/21-2023/24; budget narrative and table differ on the number of reviewed local authorities.
MoCU's full local-governance study and the World Bank's 2026 climate-shock report were not readable; repository abstract or metadata alone do not provide district-level vulnerability estimates.
Main reviewed the government audit/report, repository abstracts and IKI programme body. The programme's target denominators are not reconciled by guessing.
Kilosa resource-conflict findings are abstract-level perceptions/associations. National budget silos and local drainage gaps are not evidence of violence blocking adaptation.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
